what_this_is: The row sources a list may declare (row_sources: [{ source, id?, root?, of, match?, exclude?, paths?, text_extensions?, content?, values? }]) and the folder kind that serves each. source names the kind; optional id is its unique logical collection identity, defaulting to source for existing lists. Each template input uses the declared source fields, retaining exact JSON types; absent optional inputs are omitted. content, exclude, paths and text_extensions are forwarded unchanged. values projects fields while retaining every original value. limit and after bound each page. A refresh streams all successful pages before it removes obsolete rows, regardless of a view's rows_per_read bound. A new source kind is one row here and one in read-data/sources.mjs. A source declared original: "list" (with optional adopt_own_rows and copy_name) is the list's copy instead of its origin: its refresh is the two-way sync of list-copy.mjs, through the kind's change function, and only a kind with change and copy can be one.

restore.why: The account's restore generation (list-copy.mjs invariant 6): the setting record stamped when the account adopts an older copy of its state, { value: { generation, restored_at } }. The caller hands in that record as stored.restore, { value: { generation, restored_at } }, or null when the account was never restored. A two-way sync trusts no removal judged from a row version older than restored_at, so a restore never deletes the newer file copies: they are carried back up.

copies_when_unreachable.why: When a list's file copy may be read, read-only (copy-readable.mjs, asked by a copy guard): only when the caller's reading of the list says it answered one of these codes, or that the store cannot be reached at all (transport_failures), which is when every holder of the account is unreachable. Any answer from the list, with or without rows, keeps the copy closed, so agents read the list. On Nov 3, 2026 the account's stores were lost and the door answered original_workspace_source_unavailable for hours while the copies held every memory.

limits.why: The bounds of a list read and a refresh, kept by the list reader because reading a list is this tool's job (the caller's store holds the records and lists them; it reads no list). read_page_rows: rows a page holds when the caller names no limit, and the most one source page asks for. rows_per_read: the most rows one view read gathers, including rules or a sort; a refresh streams as many bounded pages as a source needs and is not capped at that view bound. row_sources_per_list: the most row sources one list may declare (8 since 2026-11-05: the Library declares six, its sixth the knowledge folder's hidden files by exact path, which a folder scan skips). planned_shown: the most planned actions a dry run of a two-way sync lists; its counts are always whole.

documents.about: the markdown documents in a folder the person granted; each document a row, its frontmatter its fields (tools/documents-as-list-rows). As a list's copy (original: list), tool:change-a-document-row writes a whole document or removes one only while it is still the one read; copy names the fields that hold a document's text, its parts and the identity of the file a row was made from

json-items.about: the items of one JSON file at one path (rules, checks, any objects with an id; tools/documents-as-list-rows read-data/json-items.mjs): each item a row holding its keys as they are, its JSON text copy.text; a list names its own fields (a switch, who judges the row) in its source content.list_only, and those never reach the file. As a list's copy (original: list), tool:change-a-json-item-row writes or removes one item only while it is still the one read and keeps the rest of the file
